title: Trump: In their own words: Texans vote under redrawn maps ordered by Trump
description_short: Trump: In their own words: Texans vote under redrawn maps ordered by Trump

title: Trump: FedEx sues US government, seeking ‘full refund’ over Trump tariffs
description_short: Trump: FedEx sues US government, seeking ‘full refund’ over Trump tariffs
description_medium: FedEx sued the U.S. government on February 23, 2026, seeking a full refund of tariffs imposed under Trump. The company did not specify an amount. Its suit followed a Supreme Court ruling that Trump had exceeded his authority in issuing the tariffs; FedEx said it was protecting its rights as an importer of record.
description_long: FedEx sued the U.S. government on February 23, 2026, seeking a full refund of duties it had paid under President Donald Trump’s tariffs. The company did not specify the amount it wanted returned. It filed in the U.S. Court of International Trade, naming U.S. Customs and Border Protection, the agency’s commissioner and the United States as defendants. The suit was the first attempt by a major company to recover its share of tariffs after the Supreme Court ruled that Trump had exceeded his authority in imposing them under an emergency-powers law. The Guardian reported that the ruling did not address whether companies were entitled to refunds, leaving importers to seek reimbursement through litigation. FedEx said it was taking action to protect its rights as the importer of record. The case could be followed by other businesses seeking repayment, but its filing alone did not establish an amount due or determine how the government would handle refunds.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: FedEx sues US government, seeking ‘full refund’ over Trump tariffs
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: FedEx sues US government, seeking ‘full refund’ over Trump tariffs

notes: The linked Guardian report was read directly. It supports the filing date, forum, defendants, absence of a specified refund amount, and context of the Supreme Court ruling; the description does not assume FedEx will prevail or receive a particular amount.

title: Trump: Top DHS spokesperson to exit role amid growing outrage over Trump’s ICE raids
description_short: Trump: Top DHS spokesperson to exit role amid growing outrage over Trump’s ICE raids
description_medium: The Department of Homeland Security confirmed on February 17, 2026, that spokesperson Tricia McLaughlin would leave the agency the following week. The Guardian reported that she had been one of the administration’s most visible defenders of deportation raids, amid public criticism after federal officers fatally shot Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minneapolis.
description_long: The Guardian reported on February 17, 2026, that Tricia McLaughlin, the Department of Homeland Security’s top spokesperson, would leave the agency the following week. DHS confirmed her departure. McLaughlin had been one of the most visible public defenders of the Trump administration’s deportation raids. The announcement came as the agency faced scrutiny after federal immigration officers fatally shot Alex Pretti and Renee Good in Minneapolis and public support for the enforcement push had fallen. The Guardian said McLaughlin had planned to leave in December but stayed after the shootings. She had defended the actions of federal officers, including describing Pretti as having “violently resisted” and saying officers fired defensive shots. House Democrats had filed articles of impeachment against Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, alleging violations of public trust and obstruction of congressional oversight. The article reports a spokesperson’s departure during a period of public and congressional pressure; it does not say that the criticism caused her exit.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Top DHS spokesperson to exit role amid growing outrage over Trump’s ICE raids
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Top DHS spokesperson to exit role amid growing outrage over Trump’s ICE raids

notes: The linked Guardian report was read directly. The revised text replaces generic downstream-effect claims with the departure timing, McLaughlin’s public role and the reported oversight context without claiming that criticism caused her departure.

title: Trump’s border czar warned deportations should be targeted to ‘keep faith of American people’
description_short: Trump’s border czar warned deportations should be targeted to ‘keep faith of American people’
description_medium: In a June 2025 interview reported by NBC and The Guardian on February 9, 2026, border czar Tom Homan said immigration enforcement should prioritize people who had committed additional crimes. He warned that broader operations could erode public support and said enforcement should be humane. The remarks preceded his assignment to Minnesota.
description_long: Tom Homan, whom the Trump administration later sent to Minnesota as its border czar, said in a June 2025 interview that immigration enforcement should prioritize people who had committed crimes beyond being in the country unlawfully. NBC reported the interview on February 9, 2026, as part of coverage of Homan’s forthcoming book; The Guardian summarized it the same day. Homan said that sticking to such priorities would help “keep the faith of the American people” and that broad enforcement could cost the administration public support. He also said enforcement should be carried out humanely. At the time of the interview, Border Patrol agents under Greg Bovino were conducting large-scale raids in Los Angeles, with arrests targeting immigrants based on where they lived rather than a set of identified targets. Homan’s remarks described the approach he believed would retain support; they do not show that the administration subsequently followed it. The account records a stated distinction between targeted enforcement and broad raids, not a change in policy.

preserved_fields.title: Trump’s border czar warned deportations should be targeted to ‘keep faith of American people’
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump’s border czar warned deportations should be targeted to ‘keep faith of American people’

notes: The linked Guardian and NBC reports were read directly. They support Homan’s June 2025 remarks, his stated prioritization and the Los Angeles enforcement context; the description distinguishes his recommendation from subsequent agency policy.
